ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Latent Structure Alignment for LLM Complexity Estimation
PROPOSAL: Introduce a novel framework for aligning the latent structures of language models with those of natural language data, enabling complexity estimation of texts and models at scale. By leveraging the learnable attention mechanism of LLMs, we can identify the relevant latent dimensions that contribute the most to textual structure and derive a complexity-oriented metric that captures the interactions between local textures and global hierarchies.
CONTROLS: Evaluation on existing complexity and degeneration benchmarks, e.g. BIG-Bench.
COST: 800 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Demonstrate significant improvements over existing metrics, specifically for capturing inter-model and inter-textual complexity variations, with moderate prediction power for outlier detection.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Degeneration Detection via Latent Structure Disruptions
PROPOSAL: Develop a degeneration detection framework based on identifying disruptions in the latent structure of texts generated by LLMs. Specifically, we will compute the difference between the aligned latent structures of natural texts and generated texts, leveraging the Latent Structure Alignment (LSA) framework introduced in Proposal 3. We will use this framework to identify novel metrics for measuring degeneration, focusing on key indicators such as coherence breaks, style inconsistencies, and semantic loss.
CONTROLS: Comparative analysis with existing degeneration metrics (e.g. MLE, ROUGE, BLEU).
COST: 600 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Successfully detect degeneration in a wide range of text genres, including long-form articles, chatty dialogues, and dense technical texts, with significant improvement over existing metrics.

PROPOSAL: REVISE 3: Degeneration Detection via Latent Structure Disruptions
To improve the detectability and interpretability of degeneration, we incorporate explicit measures of coherence, consistency, and semantic loss into the framework. These are added as additional latent structure metrics, which can be analyzed individually and collectively to improve the detection capabilities of the method. For example, we compute the coherence score of each input text, the consistency score of generated text compared to the input, and the semantic loss score measuring the distance between the input and generated text semantic spaces.
CONTROLS: Ablation study to examine the contribution of each additional metric to the overall degeneration detection performance.
COST: 200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Demonstrate improved degeneration detection for a wide range of text genres, with limitations revealed by the ablation study helping to prioritize further development.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Uncovering the Role of Self-Similarity in LLM Hallucinations
PROPOSAL: Investigate the relationship between self-similarity in generated text and language model hallucinations. We will use the LSA framework from Proposal 3 to analyze the latent structures of generated text exhibiting hallucinations, comparing them to those of coherent texts. We hypothesize that hallucinations will be associated with disruptions in the self-similar latent structures of the input text.
CONTROLS: A comparison with existing hallucination detection methods (e.g. fact-checking, surface-level inconsistency detection).
COST: 400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Find cases where self-similarity is a strong predictor of hallucinations, but also highlight cases where alternative explanations (e.g. gradient-based diffusion, greedy inference) contribute significantly to hallucinations.

PROPOSAL: REVISE 1: Local-Global Alignment for Safer Language Model Inference 
To better understand the impact of the proposed local-global alignment framework on inference safety, we modify the evaluation protocol to examine the performance of the aligned model on a range of text understanding and generation benchmarks, including multi-step reasoning, abductive reasoning, and consistent dialogue generation. We will compare the results to a baseline model and assess the improvement in safety and overall performance due to the local-global alignment.
CONTROLS: Comparative study with existing safety metrics (e.g. stability, faithfulness).
COST: 500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Demonstrate significantly improved results on specific benchmarks, highlighting the safety benefits of local-global alignment.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Measuring Structure-Function Tradeoffs in LLM Pre-training
PROPOSAL: Investigate the relationship between the pre-training objectives and the structure-function tradeoffs in large language models. We will use a range of analysis tools, including LSA, to examine the impact of pre-training objectives on the latent structure of the model and its downstream performance on language understanding and generation tasks.
CONTROLS: Analysis of existing pre-training objectives (e.g. masked language modeling, next sentence prediction).
COST: 700 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Find structure-function tradeoffs associated with specific pre-training objectives, highlighting the importance of understanding these tradeoffs for improved LLM performance and stability.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Role of Linguistic Universals in LLM Behavior
PROPOSAL: Examine the relationship between linguistic universals and the behavior of large language models. We will use a combination of LSA and linguistic corpora analysis to investigate how different linguistic universals (e.g. word order, grammatical case) affect the structure and function of LLMs. This will help us better understand how LLMs process language and make predictions.
CONTROLS: Analysis of linguistic corpora (e.g. Universal Dependencies) and existing LLM datasets.
COST: 900 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Find correlations between linguistic universals and specific aspects of LLM behavior, such as semantic reasoning, contextual understanding, and generation capability.

To further investigate the relationship between the pre-training objectives and the structure-function tradeoffs, we will develop a new evaluation framework that quantifies the tradeoffs in terms of multiple dimensions (e.g. reasoning, accuracy, coherence). This will enable us to better understand the impact of different pre-training objectives on the overall performance of LLMs.
CONTROLS: Comparative study with existing pre-training objectives and LLM variants.

TITLE: Relational Reasoning as a Diagnostic for LLM Complexity
PROPOSAL: Develop a relational reasoning framework for LLMs to diagnose and measure the complexity of their logical reasoning capabilities. We will use this framework to identify relationships between relational reasoning and other complex behaviors, such as question answering, decision-making, and generalization.
CONTROLS: Evaluation on a range of relational reasoning tasks and benchmarks (e.g. Visual Question Answering, LOGIQA).
COST: 1200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Find significant correlations between relational reasoning and other complex behaviors, enabling a new diagnostic for LLM complexity and potential improvements in logical reasoning and decision-making capabilities.

TITLE: Unifying Local-Global Alignment and Relational Reasoning for Comprehensive LLM Evaluation
PROPOSAL: Integrate the local-global alignment framework (Proposal 1) with the relational reasoning framework (Proposal 5) to develop a unified evaluation approach for LLMs. This will enable comprehensive assessment of both local and global structure-function tradeoffs in LLMs, facilitating a deeper understanding of their limitations and potential improvements.
CONTROLS: Comparative study with existing evaluation frameworks and LLM variants.
COST: 1800 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Demonstrate significantly improved comprehensive evaluation of LLMs, enabling more informed decision-making for LLM design, optimization, and deployment.

Note: This proposal aims to tie together the various lines of research developed in the previous proposals, providing a comprehensive and unified evaluation approach for LLMs.

PROPOSAL: Introduce a new metric, "Continuity Coefficient" (CC), measuring the degree to which a language model's local predictions are horizontally consistent with the structural properties of the text. TITLE: Evaluating Self-Similarity in LLM Outputs
PROPOSAL: Investigate self-similarity in language models through multiscale analysis of generated texts. This involves computing log-log plots of cumulative frequency distributions and examining their slope and exponent values across different scales, and testing whether self-similar properties of natural language are preserved in LLM-generated text.
CONTROLS: Self-similarity analysis on natural language texts, comparison with perplexity and CC metric, and varying model sizes and training conditions.
COST: 300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Self-similarity patterns in language models can be detected and analyzed through multiscale analysis, and may correlate with CC metric results, shedding light on the degree of internal complexity in LLMs.

TITLE: Multi-Task Training for Hallucination Detection and Degeneration Mitigation
PROPOSAL: Investigate the benefits of combining hallucination detection and degeneration mitigation tasks into a single multi-task learning objective for LLMs, using a dual-task setup with the CC-based metric. This involves incorporating both hallucination detection and degeneration metrics into the LLM's loss function, to encourage models that not only avoid degeneration but also detect and prevent hallucinations.

PROPOSAL: Further refinement of the proposal incorporates a mechanism to predict the confidence of the LLM's output, enabling the model to identify situations where it is likely to produce hallucinations or degenerate outputs. This added self-assessment capability will be achieved by training a Confidence Estimation Head (CEH) alongside the LLM, and using the CEH's output to weigh the loss contributions from hallucination detection and degeneration metrics.
CONTROLS: Comparative analysis with CEH-agnostic model variants, additional ablation experiments to examine the impact of varying CEH design choices (e.g., architecture, task type) and CEH-importance weightings on model performance, and exploration of applicability to downstream tasks requiring more nuanced uncertainty quantification.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Incorporating CEH with multi-task learning objectives is predicted to yield substantially better hallucination detection and degeneration mitigation performance, along with the ability to predict when its own outputs may be unreliable, enabling more informed decision-making or corrective actions in deployment scenarios.
